The '''49ers–Seahawks rivalry''' is a [[National Football League]] (NFL) [[List of NFL rivalries|rivalry]] between the [[San Francisco 49ers]] and [[Seattle Seahawks]]. The two teams compete in the [[NFC West]] and lie 839 miles away from each other on [[Interstate 5]]. 

Although the teams met for the first time in [[1976 NFL season|1976]], the rivalry did not begin in earnest until 2002, when Seattle was moved to the NFC West and the teams began facing each other twice in every regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Farmer |first=Sam |date=2001-05-23 |title=NFL Votes to Realign in 2002 |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2001-may-23-sp-1400-story.html |access-date=2024-01-07 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Oates |first=Bob |date=2002-02-02 |title=Schedules Will Be Balanced |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2002-feb-02-sp-nflsked02-story.html |access-date=2024-01-07 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Freeman |first=Mike |author-link=Mike Freeman (columnist) |date=May 23, 2001 |title=PRO FOOTBALL; Owners Approve N.F.L. Realignment |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2001/05/23/sports/pro-football-owners-approve-nfl-realignment.html |access-date=February 19, 2024 |website=[[New York Times]] |page=D4}}</ref> The rivalry reached new heights in the early 2010s, when the two teams began competing for [[National Football Conference|NFC]] dominance. Either Seattle or San Francisco won the NFC West in every season from 2010 to 2014, and in this era the rivalry intensified in large part due to an [[Pete Carroll–Jim Harbaugh rivalry|existing feud]] between head coaches [[Pete Carroll]] and [[Jim Harbaugh]]. Both on-field competitiveness and off-field tension culminated in the [[2013 NFC Championship Game|2014 NFC Championship]], in which Seattle narrowly defeated San Francisco en route to [[Super Bowl XLVIII|Super Bowl XLVII]]. Since and particular during Harbaugh and Carroll's tenures, the rivalry has been considered among the most heated and competitive in the NFL.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-09-12 |title=San Francisco 49ers vs. Seattle Seahawks: The NFL's best rivalry |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/san-francisco-49ers-vs-seattle-seahawks-the-nfl-s-best-rivalry-0ap1000000243131 |access-date=2026-09-03 |website=www.nfl.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Deeter |first=Baily |title=Ranking the 4 Best Rivalries in the NFL |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1674284-ranking-the-4-best-rivalries-in-the-nfl |access-date=2026-09-03 |website=bleacherreport.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-09-10 |title=NFL's Best Rivalries |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2013/09/10/nfl-best-rivalries |access-date=2026-09-03 |website=SI |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-07-08 |title=NFL's top rivalries of the 2010s: Peyton Manning, Tom Brady take top spot again |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/nfls-top-rivalries-of-the-2010s-peyton-manning-tom-brady-take-top-spot-again/ |access-date=2026-09-03 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}}</ref>

Following Harbaugh's departure, the rivalry waned as Seattle swept San Francisco in three consecutive seasons amid head coach turnover. [[Kyle Shanahan]]'s appointment as head coach allowed for increased competitiveness as Shanahan led San Francisco to their [[Super Bowl LIV|seventh]] and [[Super Bowl LVIII|eighth]] [[Super Bowl]] appearances. In the [[2022–23 NFL playoffs|2022 playoffs]], San Francisco defeated Seattle in the Wild Card round in the middle of a six-game win streak against Seattle. In the [[2025–26 NFL playoffs|2025 playoffs]], [[Mike Macdonald]]'s Seahawks blew out San Francisco before winning [[Super Bowl LX]] in [[Levi's Stadium]], the 49ers' home field.

The Seahawks lead the overall series, 33–25. The two teams have met three times in the [[National Football League playoffs|playoffs]], with Seattle winning twice.<ref name="Head2Head"/>

==History==
[[File:2004 Seahawks 49ers NFL.jpg|thumb|left|Seattle Seahawks vs. San Francisco 49ers (final score 34–0), September 26, 2004]]
Since the teams became [[NFC West]] division rivals in 2002, the rivalry has grown considerably.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Steward |first=Carl |date=2003-10-12 |title=Ports of call build budding rivalry Seattle Seahawks San Francisco 49ers |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/oakland-tribune-ports-of-call-build-budd/125939627/ |access-date=2024-02-20 |work=Oakland Tribune |pages=22}}</ref> The rivalry was previously insignificant, due to both teams having little history against one another and both suffering long stretches of mediocrity. For example, while the Seahawks won four straight division titles from 2004 to 2007, the 49ers finished in third or fourth place each season and did not have a winning season from 2003 to 2010. Likewise, the Seahawks suffered four straight losing seasons from 2008 to 2011. Despite their stretch of mediocrity, the Seahawks have remained competitive in games against the 49ers in those years.

{{quote box|width=25em
| align = left
| quote = "It don't get much better than the 49ers...it felt like a Super Bowl when we were playing during that time."
| source = —[[K. J. Wright]], Seahawks LB<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/nfl/seattle-seahawks/article235714627.html |title=Seahawks-Rams Thursday is big. But for K.J. Wright, it's not old Seahawks-49ers big |first=Gregg |last=Bell |date=October 2, 2019 |access-date=October 2, 2019 |work=[[The News Tribune]]}}</ref>
}}
The rivalry intensified in 2011, when long-standing [[Stanford–USC football rivalry|college rival]] coaches—former [[USC Trojans football|USC]] coach [[Pete Carroll]] and former [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford]] head coach [[Jim Harbaugh]]—took over as head coaches, with Carroll becoming the Seahawks' head coach in {{nfly|2010}}, and Harbaugh becoming the 49ers coach in {{nfly|2011}}. Both teams drafted young, mobile quarterbacks to lead their franchises, Seattle's [[Russell Wilson]] and San Francisco's [[Colin Kaepernick]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Farrar |first=Doug |date=December 5, 2013 |title=Second-year starting quarterbacks Kaepernick, Wilson are key men in revived Seahawks/49ers rivalry |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2013/12/05/colin-kaepernick-russell-wilson-san-francisco-49ers-seattle-seahawks |access-date=January 1, 2014}}</ref> Both coaches turned their respective franchises into perennial playoff contenders, and from 2010 to 2014, either the Seahawks or the 49ers won the NFC West championship.

The two teams met in the [[2013–14 NFL playoffs#NFC Championship Game: Seattle Seahawks 23, San Francisco 49ers 17|2013 NFC Championship Game]] in Seattle with a trip to [[Super Bowl XLVIII]] on the line, with the Seahawks winning 23–17. The game ended when Seahawks' [[cornerback]] [[Richard Sherman (American football)|Richard Sherman]], whom Harbaugh previously coached at Stanford, [[Immaculate Deflection|tipped an end zone pass]] that led to a game-ending interception. Sherman had his famous postgame interview immediately afterwards, calling out 49ers wide receiver [[Michael Crabtree]] and claiming to be the "best corner in the game".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/audibles/2014/01/19/richard-sherman-michael-crabtree-seattle-seahawks |title=Richard Sherman calls out Michael Crabtree in all-time postgame interview |last=Eagle |first=Ben |date=January 19, 2014 |website=SI.com |language=en |access-date=July 10, 2019}}</ref> Seattle went on to defeat the [[Denver Broncos]] 43–8 in Super Bowl XLVIII to win their first [[List of Super Bowl champions|Super Bowl championship]].<ref name="z059">{{cite web | last=Gittings | first=Paul | title=Seattle Seahawks wins Super Bowl for first time in its history | website=CNN | date=2014-02-03 | url=https://www.cnn.com/2014/02/02/sport/superbowl-xlviii-denver-seattle/index.html | access-date=2025-02-09}}</ref> San Francisco had represented the NFC in a losing effort in [[Super Bowl XLVII]] the previous season. In 2018, [[Richard Sherman (American football)|Richard Sherman]] joined San Francisco and took them to [[Super Bowl LIV]] while coming a quarter short sparked the rivalry for a short while then it died down again.

After drafting Russell Wilson in 2012, the Seahawks dominated the rivalry, holding a 17–4 record against the 49ers before Wilson's departure in early 2022. After Wilson's departure, the 49ers turned the rivalry around, winning six in a row, which is the longest win streak for the 49ers against the Seahawks, before the Seahawks ended the streak with a come-from-behind 20–17 victory on 17 November 2024, which [[Geno Smith]] won with a rushing touchdown 12 seconds before the end of the game. This was Smith's only victory over the 49ers, following five losses.

In the [[2025 NFL season]], the two teams met in the playoffs for the third time, and this time Seattle won 41–6.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ocenada |first1=Ryan |last2=Smith |first2=Tor |title=49ers playoff run ends after blowout loss to Seahawks |url=https://www.kron4.com/sports/49ers-lose-seahawks-nfc-divisional-playoffs/ |access-date=January 18, 2026 |work=KRON4 |date=January 17, 2026}}</ref> This game was a rematch of the Week 18 game to determine the #1 seed in the NFC, which Seattle won 13–3.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Henderson |first1=Brady |title=Seahawks ride stifling defense, secure NFC's No. 1 seed |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/47497275/seattle-seahawks-secure-nfc-no-1-seed-13-3-victory |access-date=January 18, 2026 |work=ESPN.com |date=January 4, 2026 |language=en}}</ref>
